title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 10. The Pastimes of Dance
html:
The Lord honours Haridasa and sends Advaita home; the shreds of Nityananda's kaupina; the Lord carries Srivasa away and reappears; pastimes in the mood of the gopis; the washing of the Avadhuta's feet; Haridasa and Advaita come

Verse 1

स्नात्वा द्युनद्यां जगदीशपूजां
कृत्वा समीयुः पुनरेव सन्निधौ।
विश्वम्भरस्याम्बुजलोचनस्य
सोऽपि प्रमोदेन ददर्श तान्प्रभुः॥१॥

snātvā dyunadyāṁ jagadīśapūjāṁ
kṛtvā samīyuḥ punareva sannidhau|
viśvambharasyāmbujalocanasya
so'pi pramodena dadarśa tānprabhuḥ||1||

snatva — having bathed; dyunadyam — in the heavenly river; jagat-isha-pujam — the worship of the Lord of the world; kritva — having performed; samiyuh — came; punah eva — once again; sannidhau — into the presence; vishvambharasya — of Vishvambhara; ambuja-lochanasya — the lotus-eyed; sah — He; api — too; pramodena — with delight; dadarsha — saw; tan — them; prabhuh — the Lord.

1Having bathed in the heavenly river and worshipped the Lord of the world, they came once more into the presence of lotus-eyed Vishvambhara; and the Lord too looked upon them with delight.

Verse 2

ततः परं श्रीहरिदासमुत्तमं
श्रीकृष्णपादाम्बुजमत्तषट्पदम्।
सुशीतलं साधुविलोचनोत्सवं
नवोद्गतेन्दुप्रतिमं सुमङ्गलम्॥२॥

tataḥ paraṁ śrīharidāsamuttamaṁ
śrīkṛṣṇapādāmbujamattaṣaṭpadam|
suśītalaṁ sādhuvilocanotsavaṁ
navodgatendupratimaṁ sumaṅgalam||2||

tatah param — thereafter; shri-haridasam — Sri Haridasa; uttamam — the excellent; shri-krishna-pada-ambuja-matta-shatpadam — an intoxicated bee at the lotus feet of Sri Krishna; su-shitalam — cool and soothing; sadhu-vilochana-utsavam — a festival for the eyes of the saintly; nava-udgata-indu-pratimam — like the newly risen moon; su-mangalam — most auspicious.

2Then He saw the excellent Sri Haridasa1 — an intoxicated bee at the lotus feet of Sri Krishna, cool and soothing, a festival for the eyes of the saintly, full of grace, like the newly risen moon.

Verse 3

दृष्ट्वा समालिङ्ग्य भुजद्वयेन
दृढं हरिस्तं निजपादभक्तम्।
समादिदेशासनमुग्रकीर्ति-
स्तस्मै पुनस्तं प्रणनाम सोऽपि॥३॥

dṛṣṭvā samāliṅgya bhujadvayena
dṛḍhaṁ haristaṁ nijapādabhaktam|
samādideśāsanamugrakīrti-
stasmai punastaṁ praṇanāma so'pi||3||

drishtva — seeing; samalingya — embracing; bhuja-dvayena — with both arms; dridham — tightly; harih — Hari; tam — him; nija-pada-bhaktam — the devotee of His feet; samadidesha — offered; asanam — a seat; ugra-kirtih — He of mighty fame; tasmai — to him; punah — in turn; tam — to Him; pranama — bowed; sah — he; api — too.

3Seeing him, Hari of mighty fame embraced this devotee of His feet tightly in both arms and offered him a seat; and he in turn bowed down to Him.

Verse 4

तं चन्दनेनाशु विलेपयित्वा
माल्यं च दत्त्वाथ महाप्रसादम्।
अन्नं रसैर्युक्तमनुत्तमं ददौ
चतुःप्रकारं बुभुजे तदाज्ञया॥४॥

taṁ candanenāśu vilepayitvā
mālyaṁ ca dattvātha mahāprasādam|
annaṁ rasairyuktamanuttamaṁ dadau
catuḥprakāraṁ bubhuje tadājñayā||4||

tam — him; chandanena — with sandal paste; ashu — at once; vilepayitva — having anointed; malyam — a garland; cha — and; dattva — having given; atha — then; maha-prasadam — mahaprasada; annam — food; rasaih — with flavours; yuktam — endowed; anuttamam — unsurpassed; dadau — gave; chatuh-prakaram — of four kinds; bubhuje — ate; tat-ajnaya — at His command.

4At once the Lord anointed him with sandal paste, put a garland on him and gave him mahaprasada — unsurpassed food of the four kinds2, full of every flavour; and he ate it at His command.

Verse 5

सोऽपि प्रसन्नेन्दुमुखः सुखोषितो
हरेर्गृहे राजति देववत्सुधीः।
गायन्हरेः कीर्तनमङ्गलं मुहु-
र्मुमोद नित्यात्मसुखेन धीरः॥५॥

so'pi prasannendumukhaḥ sukhoṣito
harergṛhe rājati devavatsudhīḥ|
gāyanhareḥ kīrtanamaṅgalaṁ muhu-
rmumoda nityātmasukhena dhīraḥ||5||

sah — he; api — too; prasanna-indu-mukhah — his face like a clear moon; sukha-ushitah — dwelling happily; hareh — of Hari; grihe — in the house; rajati — shines; deva-vat — like a god; sudhih — the wise; gayan — singing; hareh — of Hari; kirtana-mangalam — the auspicious glorification; muhuh — again and again; mumoda — rejoiced; nitya-atma-sukhena — in the eternal happiness of the soul; dhirah — the steadfast.

5And the wise Haridasa, his face clear as the moon, dwelt happily in Hari's house, shining like a god; steadfast, he sang again and again the auspicious praise of Hari and rejoiced in the eternal happiness of the soul.

Verse 6

तेनैव सार्धं भगवाननादिः
क्रीडां तथाचार्यसमं विधाय।
संप्रेषयामास निजालयं त-
मद्वैतसिंहोऽपि जगाम हृष्टः॥६॥

tenaiva sārdhaṁ bhagavānanādiḥ
krīḍāṁ tathācāryasamaṁ vidhāya|
saṁpreṣayāmāsa nijālayaṁ ta-
madvaitasiṁho'pi jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ||6||

tena eva — with him; sardham — together; bhagavan — Bhagavan; anadih — the beginningless; kridam — play; tatha — thus; acharya-samam — together with the Acharya; vidhaya — having held; sampreshayam asa — sent; nija-alayam — to his own abode; tam — him; advaita-simhah — the lion Advaita; api — too; jagama — went; hrishtah — joyful.

6The beginningless Bhagavan made merry thus with him, together with the Acharya, and sent him to his own abode; and the lion Advaita too went away rejoicing.

Verse 7

ततोऽवधूतं विनयेन धीरो
गच्छन्ननुव्रज्य सुदूरमीशः।
उवाच कौपीनकचेलमेकं
देहि त्वमेभ्यो द्विजसज्जनेभ्यः॥७॥

tato'vadhūtaṁ vinayena dhīro
gacchannanuvrajya sudūramīśaḥ|
uvāca kaupīnakacelamekaṁ
dehi tvamebhyo dvijasajjanebhyaḥ||7||

tatah — then; avadhutam — the Avadhuta; vinayena — humbly; dhirah — the composed; gachchhan — going; anuvrajya — having escorted; su-duram — far; ishah — the Lord; uvacha — said; kaupinaka-chelam — a cloth of kaupina; ekam — one; dehi — give; tvam — you; ebhyah — to these; dvija-sat-janebhyah — noble brahmanas.

7Then the Lord, humble and composed, escorted the departing Avadhuta a long way and said to Him: "Give these noble brahmanas one cloth of Your kaupina3."

Verse 8

ददौ तदा तद्वचनेच्छया स
कौपीनमेकं तदसौ गृहीत्वा।
स्वयं प्रभुर्भृत्यजनाय चेलं
ददौ विभज्य प्रतिगृह्य ते मुदा॥८॥

dadau tadā tadvacanecchayā sa
kaupīnamekaṁ tadasau gṛhītvā|
svayaṁ prabhurbhṛtyajanāya celaṁ
dadau vibhajya pratigṛhya te mudā||8||

dadau — gave; tada — then; tat-vachana-ichchhaya — according to the wish of His words; sah — he; kaupinam — kaupina; ekam — one; tat — it; asau — He; grihitva — taking; svayam — Himself; prabhuh — the Lord; bhritya-janaya — to His servants; chelam — the cloth; dadau — gave; vibhajya — having divided; pratigrihya — having received; te — they; muda — joyfully.

8Then, to fulfil the wish of His words, He gave Him a kaupina; the Lord took it, divided the cloth Himself and gave the pieces to His servants. Joyfully receiving them,

Verse 9

विधाय मौलौ नृहरेः प्रसादं
कृष्णेन सार्धं निजमेव मन्दिरम्।
आगत्य ते प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्या
निपत्य भूमौ रुरुदुः सुदुःखिताः॥९॥

vidhāya maulau nṛhareḥ prasādaṁ
kṛṣṇena sārdhaṁ nijameva mandiram|
āgatya te premavibhinnadhairyā
nipatya bhūmau ruruduḥ suduḥkhitāḥ||9||

vidhaya — placing; maulau — on their heads; nrihareh — of Nrihari; prasadam — the gift of grace; krishnena — with Krishna; sardham — together; nijam eva — to His own; mandiram — house; agatya — having come; te — they; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — their composure broken by love; nipatya — falling; bhumau — to the ground; ruruduh — wept; su-duhkhitah — deeply grieved.

9they placed this gift of Nrihari's grace on their heads and came with Krishna to His house; and there, all composure broken by love, they fell to the ground and wept in deep grief.

Verse 10

ततो निमज्याम्भसि भूमिदेवाः
स्नात्वा द्युनद्यां हरिपूजनक्रियाम्।
चक्रुः पुनः सायमुपागतास्ते
विजह्रुरार्या हरिणा समं जगुः॥१०॥

tato nimajyāmbhasi bhūmidevāḥ
snātvā dyunadyāṁ haripūjanakriyām|
cakruḥ punaḥ sāyamupāgatāste
vijahrurāryā hariṇā samaṁ jaguḥ||10||

tatah — then; nimajya — plunging; ambhasi — into the water; bhumi-devah — the brahmanas ("gods on earth"); snatva — having bathed; dyunadyam — in the heavenly river; hari-pujana-kriyam — the rite of worshipping Hari; chakruh — performed; punah — again; sayam — in the evening; upagatah — having come; te — they; vijahruh — sported; aryah — the noble; harina — with Hari; samam — together; jaguh — sang.

10Then the brahmanas, the "gods on earth," plunged into the waters of the heavenly river, bathed and performed the rite of worshipping Hari; and in the evening they came again, and the noble ones made merry and sang together with Hari.

Verse 11

आलिङ्ग्य भृत्यानपि तान्गृहीत्वा
भूमौ लुठत्यब्जकरद्वयेन।
आनन्दमत्यर्थमनन्तकीर्तिः
समुद्वहन्सिंहगतिर्ननर्त॥११॥

āliṅgya bhṛtyānapi tāngṛhītvā
bhūmau luṭhatyabjakaradvayena|
ānandamatyarthamanantakīrtiḥ
samudvahansiṁhagatirnanarta||11||

alingya — embracing; bhrityan — His servants; api — even; tan — them; grihitva — clasping; bhumau — on the ground; luthati — rolls; abja-kara-dvayena — with His two lotus hands; anandam — bliss; ati-artham — boundless; ananta-kirtih — He of endless fame; samudvahan — bearing; simha-gatih — with a lion's gait; nanarta — danced.

11Embracing His servants and clasping them in His two lotus hands, He of endless fame rolls upon the ground; and, bearing boundless bliss within Him, He danced with the gait of a lion.

Verse 12

श्रीवासमादाय भुजद्वयेन
तन्मध्यतो दूरतरं निनाय।
ततो न दृष्ट्वा विवशा बभूवुः
सविस्मितास्ते हरिदासवर्याः॥१२॥

śrīvāsamādāya bhujadvayena
tanmadhyato dūrataraṁ nināya|
tato na dṛṣṭvā vivaśā babhūvuḥ
savismitāste haridāsavaryāḥ||12||

shrivasam — Srivasa; adaya — taking up; bhuja-dvayena — in both arms; tat-madhyatah — from their midst; durataram — far away; ninaya — carried; tatah — then; na drishtva — not seeing (Him); vivashah — helpless; babhuvuh — became; sa-vismitah — amazed; te — those; hari-dasa-varyah — best of Hari's servants.

12Taking up Srivasa in both arms, He carried him far away from their midst; and, not seeing Him, those best of Hari's servants were bewildered and amazed.

Verse 13

विचार्य ते नो ददृशुर्महान्तः
क्षुब्धान्विदित्वा तदजः समागतः।
स्वयं स्वतन्त्रार्थरतः पुरस्ता-
त्ते पार्श्वतस्तं परिवव्रुरुत्सुकाः॥१३॥

vicārya te no dadṛśurmahāntaḥ
kṣubdhānviditvā tadajaḥ samāgataḥ|
svayaṁ svatantrārtharataḥ purastā-
tte pārśvatastaṁ parivavrurutsukāḥ||13||

vicharya — searching; te — they; no dadrishuh — did not find; maha-antah — the great souls; kshubdhan — distressed; viditva — knowing (them); tat — then; ajah — the Unborn; samagatah — came; svayam — Himself; svatantra-artha-ratah — delighting in His own free will; purastat — before (them); te — they; parshvatah — on all sides; tam — Him; parivavruh — surrounded; utsukah — eagerly.

13The great souls searched but did not find Him. Knowing that they were troubled, the Unborn, who delights in His own free will, Himself appeared before them, and they eagerly crowded round Him on every side.

Verse 14

गोपीस्वभावाप्तसमस्तभक्त्या
पश्यंश्च कृष्णं वनमालिनं प्रभुम्।
मद्वल्लभोऽसौ भगवान्यथा भवे-
त्तथा कृपां मे कुरुतान्महेश्वरः॥१४॥

gopīsvabhāvāptasamastabhaktyā
paśyaṁśca kṛṣṇaṁ vanamālinaṁ prabhum|
madvallabho'sau bhagavānyathā bhave-
ttathā kṛpāṁ me kurutānmaheśvaraḥ||14||

gopi-svabhava-apta-samasta-bhaktya — with entire devotion gained through the nature of the gopis; pashyan — seeing; cha — and; krishnam — Krishna; vana-malinam — wearing the forest garland; prabhum — the Lord; mat-vallabhah — my beloved; asau — this; bhagavan — Bhagavan; yatha — so that; bhavet — may become; tatha — so; kripam — grace; me — to me; kurutat — may He show; maha-ishvarah — the Great Lord.

14And each of them, looking with entire devotion, gained through the nature of the gopis, upon Krishna, the Lord with the forest garland, prayed: "May the Great Lord4 show me grace, so that this Bhagavan may become my beloved!"

Verse 15

गोपाङ्गनाभावविभावनिष्ठः
श्रीकृष्ण एवात्र रसेन पूर्णः।
गोपस्त्रीभावान्प्रणतान्विभाव्य
करोति वस्त्राहरणादिलीलाम्॥१५॥

gopāṅganābhāvavibhāvaniṣṭhaḥ
śrīkṛṣṇa evātra rasena pūrṇaḥ|
gopastrībhāvānpraṇatānvibhāvya
karoti vastrāharaṇādilīlām||15||

gopa-angana-bhava-vibhava-nishthah — intent on awakening the feeling of the cowherd women; shri-krishnah — Sri Krishna; eva — Himself; atra — here; rasena — with rasa; purnah — filled; gopa-stri-bhavan — possessed of the feeling of the cowherd women; pranatan — bowing (to Him); vibhavya — perceiving; karoti — performs; vastra-aharana-adi-lilam — the pastime of stealing the garments and others.

15For here is Sri Krishna Himself, full of rasa and wholly intent on awakening the feeling of the cowherd women. Perceiving in the devotees who bowed before Him the feeling of the gopis, He performs the pastime of stealing the garments5 and other pastimes.

Verse 16

ततः कदाचिद्रजनीमुखे स
वस्त्रान्समाकृष्य विनग्नभावान्।
चक्रे कराम्भोजयुगेन चक्री
भृत्यान्रसज्ञो रसदो नराणाम्॥१६॥

tataḥ kadācidrajanīmukhe sa
vastrānsamākṛṣya vinagnabhāvān|
cakre karāmbhojayugena cakrī
bhṛtyānrasajño rasado narāṇām||16||

tatah — then; kadachit — once; rajani-mukhe — at nightfall; sah — He; vastran — the garments; samakrishya — pulling off; vinagna-bhavan — naked; chakre — made; kara-ambhoja-yugena — with His two lotus hands; chakri — the Holder of the discus; bhrityan — His servants; rasa-jnah — the knower of rasa; rasa-dah — the giver of rasa; naranam — to men.

16And so once, at nightfall, the Holder of the discus — the knower of rasa, the giver of rasa to men — pulled the garments off His servants with His two lotus hands and left them naked.

Verse 17

एवं प्रभुः क्रीडनकं स कृत्वा
क्षणाद्ददौ वस्त्रगणान्समस्तान्।
तेभ्यः पुनस्ते परिधाय हृष्टा
वासांसि साकं जहृषुर्मुरारिणा॥१७॥

evaṁ prabhuḥ krīḍanakaṁ sa kṛtvā
kṣaṇāddadau vastragaṇānsamastān|
tebhyaḥ punaste paridhāya hṛṣṭā
vāsāṁsi sākaṁ jahṛṣurmurāriṇā||17||

evam — thus; prabhuh — the Lord; kridanakam — a game; sah — He; kritva — having made; kshanat — in a moment; dadau — gave; vastra-ganan — the garments; samastan — all; tebhyah — to them; punah — back; te — they; paridhaya — putting on; hrishtah — glad; vasamsi — the garments; sakam — together; jahrishuh — rejoiced; murarina — with Murari.

17Having played this game, in a moment the Lord gave back all their garments; and they gladly put them on again and made merry together with Murari6.

Verse 18

गायन्हरेर्नाम पुनर्ननर्त
तैः सार्धमन्तःकरणैर्यथार्थैः।
लीलागतिर्लोकमलं क्षपन्स
सन्तप्तचामीकररोचिषा प्रभुः॥१८॥

gāyanharernāma punarnanarta
taiḥ sārdhamantaḥkaraṇairyathārthaiḥ|
līlāgatirlokamalaṁ kṣapansa
santaptacāmīkararociṣā prabhuḥ||18||

gayan — singing; hareh — of Hari; nama — the name; punah — again; nanarta — danced; taih — with them; sardham — together; antah-karanaih — whose hearts; yatha-arthaih — were sincere; lila-gatih — with a playful gait; loka-malam — the impurity of the world; kshapan — destroying; sah — He; santapta-chamikara-rochisha — with the lustre of molten gold; prabhuh — the Lord.

18Singing the name of Hari, He danced again with them, pure of heart — the Lord of playful gait, whose lustre of molten gold destroys the impurity of the world.

Verse 19

ततोऽवधूतः पुनरागतः सुखं
रेमे ननर्ताशु जगौ हरेर्गुणान्।
कृष्णेन सार्धं हलिना यथार्भकाः
पुरा तथैवात्र च वारिजेक्षणः॥१९॥

tato'vadhūtaḥ punarāgataḥ sukhaṁ
reme nanartāśu jagau harerguṇān|
kṛṣṇena sārdhaṁ halinā yathārbhakāḥ
purā tathaivātra ca vārijekṣaṇaḥ||19||

tatah — then; avadhutah — the Avadhuta; punah — again; agatah — having come; sukham — happily; reme — made merry; nanarta — danced; ashu — at once; jagau — sang; hareh — of Hari; gunan — the qualities; krishnena — with Krishna; sardham — together; halina — with the Plough-bearer; yatha — as; arbhakah — the boys; pura — of old; tatha eva — just so; atra — here; cha — and; varija-ikshanah — the Lotus-eyed.

19Then the Avadhuta came again and, happy, made merry; at once He broke into dance and sang of Hari's qualities. As once the cowherd boys played with Krishna and the Plough-bearer7, so here too did the Lotus-eyed One.

Verse 20

नृत्यावसाने भगवान्द्विजाग्र्या-
नुवाच पादाववधूतकस्य।
प्रक्षाल्य गृह्णन्तु जलं भवन्त-
श्चक्रुस्ततस्ते शिरसा तदाज्ञाम्॥२०॥

nṛtyāvasāne bhagavāndvijāgryā-
nuvāca pādāvavadhūtakasya|
prakṣālya gṛhṇantu jalaṁ bhavanta-
ścakrustataste śirasā tadājñām||20||

nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dvija-agryan — to the foremost brahmanas; uvacha — said; padau — the feet; avadhutakasya — of the Avadhuta; prakshalya — having washed; grihnantu — let take; jalam — the water; bhavantah — you; chakruh — carried out; tatah — then; te — they; shirasa — with their heads (reverently); tat-ajnam — His command.

✦

Notes

  1. Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura, the great devotee of the holy name.
  2. The four kinds of food are those that are chewed, sucked, licked and drunk.
  3. A kaupina is a renunciate's loincloth. The Lord gave the shreds of Nityananda's kaupina to the devotees as a sacred relic.
  4. The Great Lord (Maheshvara) is probably Shiva, the greatest of Vaishnavas: so the gopis of Vraja prayed to Katyayani that Krishna might become their husband (Bhagavata Purana 10.22.4).
  5. The stealing of the garments is Krishna's pastime in Vrindavana, when He carried off the clothes of the bathing gopis; here the Lord repeats it with devotees in whom the feeling of the gopis has awakened. It is a pastime of pure prema, not a worldly prank: according to the Bhagavata Purana (10.22), Krishna thereby fulfils the gopis' vow and desire and removes the last barrier between them and Himself; and here He simply responds to the feeling of the gopis that He Himself has awakened in the devotees (vv. 14–15).
  6. "Murari" ("Enemy of Mura") is here apparently an epithet of the Lord; it may also be understood as "together with Murari Gupta."
  7. The Plough-bearer is Balarama. Nityananda (Balarama) and Gaura (Krishna) play with the devotees as once with the cowherd boys of Vrindavana.
  8. The Lord; it may also be understood that Nityananda rejoiced in the speech, gait, laughter and glances of the Lotus-eyed One.
  9. The Thirty (tridasha) are the gods, conventionally thirty-three in number.
